hero.headline: The agentic royalty platform for the modern music rights economy.
hero.subhead: Debaser knows the music industry. It unites catalogue owners, manages statements, handles contracts, catches what no one has time to check by hand, and traces global royalty claims... all for those who have a claim.

problem.headline: Royalty administration. It's a messy business.

items.title: Statements don't speak the same language.
items.description: CSV from one DSP, PDF from another, a portal export that never quite matches last quarter. Every source describes the same money differently.

items.title: The contract and the payment live in different worlds.
items.description: Rates, splits, territories and deductions sit in a PDF no system has ever read. So someone re-keys the numbers by hand leaving open to potential errors.

items.title: Metadata breaks before the money moves.
items.description: A missing ISRC. A misspelled artist name. A recording filed under three different titles. The income arrives; it just can't find its way home.

items.title: Artists ask questions finance can't answer quickly.
items.description: "Why did my income drop 30%?" is a fair question. Answering it shouldn't take a week and a spreadsheet buried in someone's inbox.

items.title: Missing income is found late, if it's found at all.
items.description: Underpayments go unchallenged. Collections owed from overseas societies are never chased. Most teams don't have the hours to go looking.

productFlow.headline: New rails for a new generation of catalogue owners.
productFlow.subhead: Debaser turns messy inputs into a workflow you can actually trust. Every step backed by the source it came from.

steps.label: Ingest
steps.description: Statements, contracts and catalogue data from CSV, PDF, portal export, APIs. It doesn't matter how it arrives.

steps.label: Match
steps.description: Every payment linked to the ISRC, work, writer and split it actually belongs to.
steps.detail: ISRC · ISWC · Work codes · Party IDs

steps.label: Analyse
steps.description: Anomalies, missed income, and contract conflicts are surfaced before they become somebody's problem.

steps.label: Explain
steps.description: Any payment question, answered with the row, clause or file it came from. No guesswork.
steps.detail: Source rows · Contract clauses · Audit trail

steps.label: Resolve
steps.description: Every issue becomes an action: prepare the claim, approve the payment, close it out before statements go anywhere.

agents.headline: The royalty work nobody wants to do manually.

items.name: Ingestion Agent
items.description: Takes whatever format a CSV, PDF, export or portal throws at it, and maps it into one clean schema.

items.name: Contract Agent
items.description: Reads the contract PDF nobody else has time to: rates, splits, territories, recoupment... the lot.

items.name: Matching Agent
items.description: Matches income to the right ISRC, work, writer and recording across the whole catalogue.

items.name: Exception Agent
items.description: Catches the duplicate, the missing split, the income that quietly disappeared.

items.name: Audit Agent
items.description: Checks what you expected against what actually landed, territory by territory, and builds the case for what's missing.

items.name: Ops Agent
items.description: Turns a royalty run into a list your team can actually work through before a payment goes out.

useCases.headline: Built for the people behind the catalogue.

items.headline: Reconcile before statements go out.
items.description: Match distributor and DSP income to your catalogue, and catch the discrepancy before it reaches an artist's statement.

items.headline: Contracts and income in one place.
items.description: Works, writers, splits and income are read against the actual contract, not a spreadsheet's memory of it.

items.headline: Monitor every acquisition.
items.description: Track performance and missing income across every acquisition at the scale acquisitions actually happen.

items.headline: Audit income with evidence.
items.description: Challenge a bad statement with the row it's wrong on, not a hunch.

items.headline: Compare usage, claims and collections.
items.description: See the gap between what was claimed and what actually came back, territory by territory.

missingMoney.headline: Find the money that never made it home.
missingMoney.subhead: Debaser compares what your catalogue should be earning against what actually arrived, and tells you exactly where the gap is.
features: Usage compared against income, line by line

explainability.headline: Every number should be able to defend itself.
explainability.body1: Ask why a number changed, and Debaser traces the answer back to the row, the metadata, the clause to dig out the real cause, where ever it lies.
explainability.body2: Not a summary. Not a guess dressed up as an answer. A structured explanation with the evidence attached, so your team can check it, not just trust it.
explainability.chatUserMessage: Why did this artist earn less this quarter?
explainability.chatAiResponse: Spotify UK income dropped 31% versus Q1. Two tracks were unmatched due to missing ISRCs, accounting for roughly £3,100 in unattributed income. The producer deduction was also applied before the recoupment threshold, which conflicts with clause 4.2(b) of the recording agreement.

trust.headline: Built for data this sensitive.
trust.subhead: Royalty data is some of the most commercially sensitive information in music. We built accordingly.

items.title: Role-based access
items.description: Control exactly who sees what; by catalogue, territory, deal type or run stage.

items.title: Audit trails
items.description: Every action is logged with a timestamp and a name. Every output traces back to its source.

items.title: Every answer, sourced
items.description: Nothing ships without evidence. Every answer points back to the row, document or clause it came from.

items.title: Human approval workflows
items.description: Software flags and investigates. A human reviews and approves. No royalty run goes out without sign-off.

items.title: Private workspaces
items.description: Your data stays yours. Isolated tenancy, no cross-client data access by design.

items.title: Exportable evidence
items.description: Every claim and discrepancy exports in a format your legal and finance teams can actually use.

items.title: Designed for compliance
items.description: Built to the governance standards serious music companies already expect.

items.title: Transparent outputs
items.description: Every recommendation comes with its confidence level, its reasoning, and the raw source behind it.

vision.headline: A global ledger of who's owed what, everywhere music is used.
vision.body1: We see a world where a single graph connects every song, recording, release, contract, owner, use and payment, everywhere, for every revenue stream.
vision.body2: Debaser is starting on the operational layer, where statements pile up, income goes missing, and teams are buried in work that shouldn't need a human at all.
vision.graphCaption: Songs → Recordings → Contracts → Income → Ownership → Usage

earlyAccess.headline: Too much money moves through here to run it blind.
earlyAccess.body: We're working with a small group of labels, publishers and catalogue owners to get this right before we open it up. If statements are taking too long, or money keeps going missing without explanation, talk to us.

valueProps.title: Direct access to the team
valueProps.text: You'll work with us directly while we build this, not a support queue.

valueProps.title: Shape what we build
valueProps.text: Your royalty problems become our roadmap.

valueProps.title: Founding customer terms
valueProps.text: Early partners keep their terms as we grow. That doesn't change later.

earlyAccess.problemLabel: What royalty problem are you trying to solve?
earlyAccess.disclaimer: No spam. We'll reach out directly, one human to another.
earlyAccess.successBody: Thanks — we'll be in touch shortly to learn about your royalty operations and how we can help.

footer.tagline: The back office that finally works in the artist's favour.
footer.principle: Software investigates. Humans approve. Deterministic engines calculate.
